questions.q: Why do ACID transaction guarantees transfer across SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, per this lesson?
options: All four platforms use identical source code for transaction handling
Transactions are optional in relational databases, so this doesn't matter
Every serious relational database implements atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability as a shared contract, even though the implementation details differ
ACID only applies to SQL Server and Oracle, not open-source platforms
questions.explain: ACID is a guarantee shared across serious relational platforms, even though how each one implements isolation under the hood differs.

questions.q: Why is normalization theory (1NF, 2NF, 3NF) described as transferring directly, per this lesson?
options: It is relational modeling theory independent of any vendor, not something SQL Server invented
Normalization rules are different in every database platform
Only SQL Server supports normalized schemas
Normalization is a MySQL-specific feature
questions.explain: Normal forms and denormalization tradeoffs are schema design discipline that applies the same way regardless of which platform stores the schema.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about SQL Server's sys.databases and sys.dm_exec_requests when moving to Oracle?
options: Oracle has no system catalog at all
sys.databases works identically in Oracle without modification
Oracle uses the exact same object names
They have no direct equivalent by that exact name — Oracle uses things like DBA_TABLES and V$SESSION instead
questions.explain: Querying metadata is a transferable skill, but the specific catalog object names are platform-specific and don't carry over by name.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against thinking of RMAN as 'BACKUP DATABASE with different keywords'?
options: RMAN is an entirely different tool with its own scripting language, catalog concept, and recovery workflow
RMAN only works with SQL Server, not Oracle
SQL Server backup syntax works unmodified in RMAN
RMAN and BACKUP DATABASE are actually interchangeable commands
questions.explain: Knowing SQL Server backup syntax gives no real head start on RMAN, because RMAN is architecturally and syntactically a different tool.

questions.q: What practical habit does the lesson recommend for sorting new information while learning a new platform?
options: Ask whether it's a fact about how relational databases work in general, or a fact about how this specific vendor built their product
Only learn syntax and skip architecture entirely
Assume everything maps one-to-one to a SQL Server equivalent
Memorize every system catalog name across all platforms before starting
questions.explain: This question distinguishes permanent, transferable knowledge from platform-specific detail that shouldn't be assumed to generalize.
